dedupe_keys.name: enhancing the competitiveness of inland waterway transport a multi methodological approach applied to port barge congestion and urban areas

description: Shobayo, Peter and colleagues publish this resource through the source community. A completed thesis combines an operational survey, agent-based modelling, economic assessment and social cost-benefit analysis to examine barge congestion and urban freight. Coverage includes modular mobile terminals at Antwerp-Bruges and Rotterdam and a small-vessel urban-delivery concept. The source reports scenario-optimal terminal numbers and differences between private and welfare cost comparisons. The related time-savings/cost-model paper supports this appraisal. Proposed terminals are modelled investments, not claimed installed assets, and the results depend on cargo volume, seasonality and the valuations used. Zenodo supplies the descriptive publication with open access under cc-by-4.0. The publication does not establish public access to an implementation or its separate licence. A limitation is that complete implementation or measurement settings cannot be reconstructed from descriptive metadata alone. Related experimental components and publications retain their distinct roles; separate deposits are not assumed to provide independent observations.
